did_you_know.text: Did you know? The prophecy concerning Tyre was given in the eleventh year, in the first month, as stated in the chapter’s opening.
Did you know? Tyre rejoiced over Jerusalem’s destruction because it believed the city’s downfall would allow it to benefit from Jerusalem’s influence and trade.
Did you know? The LORD compares the many nations that will come against Tyre to waves of the sea—a picture emphasizing their power and number.
Did you know? The judgment described for Tyre includes the destruction of its walls and towers, the removal of its rubble, and its being left as a “bare rock”—exposed and desolate.
Did you know? Tyre is described as a “place for spreading fishing nets” in the sea, and it will become plunder for the nations.

Did you know? The prophet explicitly names Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon as the leader of the army that will come against Tyre from the north, along with horses, chariots, horsemen, and a great army.
Did you know? The siege description includes a siege ramp, a rampart, and shields—military measures intended to protect the attackers and bring them closer to the city walls.
Did you know? After Tyre is conquered, its wealth will be plundered and its houses destroyed; even its stones, timber, and rubble will be thrown into the water.
Did you know? One consequence of Tyre’s destruction is the end of its rejoicing: the sound of its songs and harps will no longer be heard.

Did you know? Tyre’s downfall also affects the peoples of the sea and the islands: their rulers come down from their thrones, remove their splendid garments, and mourn over the city that was powerful and terrifying on the sea.
